question: Should OpenClaw expose `referenceContext` and `reference-context` as public plugin SDK surface now, mark the lane experimental, or keep only a narrower internal Codex projection until the cross-host contract is designed?
rationale: The implementation is technically plausible and well proven, but it changes public plugin SDK and prompt-authority semantics that automation cannot bless without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Close until sponsored
options.body: Close this contributor PR now, keep the canonical issue open, and invite a maintainer-sponsored PR once the API direction is chosen.

options.title: Sponsor experimental SDK lane
options.body: A maintainer can ask for explicit experimental wording, docs, upgrade expectations, and final review before merging this direction.

options.title: Sponsor stable SDK lane
options.body: A maintainer can accept the compatibility and security-boundary commitment and proceed with this public SDK shape after final review.

recommendation.title: Close until sponsored
recommendation.body: Close this contributor PR now, keep the canonical issue open, and invite a maintainer-sponsored PR once the API direction is chosen.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the context-engine public API contract, and the history points most strongly to jalehman on that surface.
